subject: Renewal discussion: smoothing retainer & capacity offset for Atlas Labs
messages:
From: Samir Patel <s.patel@atlaslabs.ai>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 23 Nov 2026 13:12:00 -0500
Subject: Renewal discussion: smoothing retainer & credits
Attachments: usage_report_Q3.csv

Hi Rachel,

Thanks again for the pilot support this year — the model performance has been great. We're starting renewal planning and I wanted to surface a couple of asks before the formal term sheet:

- We had two large inference spikes in Q3 tied to product launches. Those transient bursts make forecasting commit levels painful; we'd like a short smoothing retainer that lets us average usage for billing for the first 3 months of the new term.
- Given budget cycles, can Redwood offer a temporary price hold (6 months) while we finalize capacity commitments?
- As a signal of intent we're open to a modest multi-month commit increase, but we'd request a one-time credit (or equivalent discount) applied as an offset to the smoothing retainer. Target goal: limit first-quarter overage variability.

I've attached a compact usage report to show the burst patterns. High level ask: can you work up a practical structure (numbers + legal mechanics) we can route to procurement this week? We have internal signoff to move quickly if the math is reasonable.

Best,
Samir
Samir Patel
Head of Infrastructure, Atlas Labs
samir.patel@atlaslabs.ai

From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 23 Nov 2026 13:45:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: Renewal discussion: smoothing retainer & credits
Attachments: redwood_proposal_v3.pdf

Team — forwarding Atlas' note and usage extract. Quick read: they want a 3-month smoothing retainer, a short price hold window, and a one-time credit applied as an offset. They indicated procurement wants numbers this week.

Proposed internal approach (first pass):
- Offer a 3-month smoothing retainer equal to 15–20% of their average monthly run rate (flexible to their preference). Retainer would be billed up front and drawn down against overages.
- Provide a price hold for 6 months on current committed rate while they ramp to a higher commit level.
- One-time credit: we can offer a drawdown credit equal to ~8–10% of their new ARR if they sign a 12-month renewal with a 15% commit increase. Credit to apply against the retainer or future invoices.

Please validate: Ben — does the % math keep margin within our threshold? Markus — any legal/legal ops flags for a retainer-with-drawdown amendment? Grace — will CS be able to operationalize burst-to-retainer conversion for the first quarter?

If we can agree on numbers I'll spin this into a short amendment and send Atlas a DocuSign-ready proposal.

Thanks,
Rachel
Rachel Kim
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Renewal discussion: smoothing retainer & credits
Attachments: pricing_calc_Atlas_v2.xlsx

On Mon, Nov 23, 2026 at 1:45 PM Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com> wrote:
> Team — forwarding Atlas' note and usage extract. Quick read: they want a 3-month smoothing retainer, a short price hold window, and a one-time credit applied as an offset. They indicated procurement wants numbers this week.

Numbers, from finance sanity check (first pass):
- If Atlas increases commit by 15% (YR1 vs current run-rate), we can offer a 7% discount off list for the renewal year and still meet margin targets.
- Recommend smoothing retainer = 20% of expected monthly run-rate (billed monthly or prepaid — prefer prepaid month-1). This gives a predictable drawdown buffer for Q1 spikes.
- One-time credit = 8% of new ARR delivered as an account credit (applied to retainer or invoices, non-refundable).
- Price hold: 6 months is okay; we should gate the hold on the signed amendment and the 15% commit increase.

Risks / asks: finance needs explicit language on how unused retainer funds are handled (expire vs roll-forward) — I suggest unused retainer rolls forward as bill credit for the remainder of the term. If we go beyond 10% effective concession (discount + credit), I'll need approval from the revenue ops director.

I'm attaching a short calc sheet showing margin impact across three smoothing retainer sizes. If we want to be more competitive, room to move credit to 10% but that eats into NPV.

Ben
Ben Carter
Head of Strategic Sales Operations, Redwood Inference

----
From: Samir Patel <s.patel@atlaslabs.ai>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>, accounts@atlaslabs.ai
Date: Fri, 27 Nov 2026 09:32:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: Renewal discussion: smoothing retainer & credits

Rachel / team — thanks for the quick turnaround and the numbers. Procurement reviewed Ben's calc and we can accept the overall structure with one tweak:

- Reduce the smoothing retainer target to 15% of expected monthly run-rate (vs 20%) to keep cashflow aligned to our internal forecast.
- We'd like the option to convert any unused retainer balance into burst-capacity credits (rather than an unspecified roll-forward), specifically for short-term launches in Q1.

If you can reflect those two items in the amendment we can sign. I'll route to legal and hope to execute via DocuSign this week: https://docusign.example/ATL-2026-003

Can you confirm final numbers in writing (credit %, retainer amount, price-hold dates) and send the DocuSign link? We aim to have this signed by 2026-11-30 to align with our budget window.

Appreciate it — Samir
